target_customer: Mobile-first individuals and small businesses in India who need to scan, edit, store and share documents on a smartphone
problem: India's small businesses run on documents but mostly have only a phone, not a desktop. India blocked the popular CamScanner app in June 2020, leaving a gap for a trusted local scanner and document suite.
business_model: Freemium consumer and SMB mobile app suite with a paid subscription tier (company states roughly 15 USD per year) and pay per use AI tools
product_category: Mobile document scanner and office suite

founders.name: Snehanshu Gandhi
previous_startups: Describes himself as a 3X entrepreneur; earlier ventures not named on the YC page
founders.background_notes: Education as stated on his YC profile. Prior employers not listed.

founders.name: Gaurav Shrishrimal
previous_startups: Second time founder per YC page; earlier venture not named

competitors.name: CamScanner
competitors.what: Chinese mobile document scanner app that dominated India before the government blocked it in June 2020
competitors.traction_then: Very large Indian user base before the block; Kaagaz positioned itself as the Indian alternative
competitors.funding_then: Owned by a Chinese company, not researched

technical_complexity.rationale: Document scanning, PDF tools and cloud storage on mobile are well understood; the hard parts were edge detection quality and scale to millions of installs on low end phones.

defensibility.rationale: Scanning features are copyable. Some stickiness from stored documents and a local trusted brand, but Google and Adobe offer free scanners.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent buying or copying Kaagaz; the company remains independent per the YC page.

market_need_then: CamScanner's June 2020 block in India created sudden demand; the founders cite more than 200 million small businesses in India and 3 million users by YC time.

branding.domain_note: Uses kaagaz.app, not a .com. A different brand sells Kaagaz rolling papers, which is a naming collision.

identity.logo: Not described in any source opened
identity.voice_and_tone: Simple, practical and inclusive; copy mixes English with Hindi phrasing and the line 'Built for Bharat' on the company site.

branding.brand_signature: Positioning as the made in India CamScanner alternative, launched right after the 2020 ban
branding.community_and_virality: Press covered 1 lakh downloads in 24 hours and 1 million downloads in under two months in 2020 (news headlines in search results).

brand_strength.rationale: Brand rode a news moment and a local meaning word (kaagaz is a Hindi word for paper per general usage, not a cited source). No sources on logo, mascot or community beyond downloads.

outcome_analysis: Kaagaz launched a free scanner a day after India blocked CamScanner in 2020, which gave it a one time distribution tailwind and millions of installs. It raised a small seed in November 2020, joined YC in Winter 2022, and reports 3 million users and 60,000 paying users at the time of the batch. It remains active and has widened into a poster and AI suite. No outcome event such as an exit or shutdown was found.
notes: Seed round amount stated as about 575,000 USD (INR 4.25 crore per Bar and Bench); YourStory page returned 403 so details come from the search result headlines of Inc42, YourStory, Inshorts and Bar and Bench. An earlier pre-seed from First Cheque and Axilor is reported without amount or date. Goodwater Capital is named as a backer only in the company's own YC description. CB Insights total of 1.08M USD and a Signalbase 1.1M USD item are unverified. Ordenado Labs Pvt Ltd is the legal entity. Marketing claims that developers are IIT Kanpur alumni appear on store pages and conflict with the YC page's IIT Bombay for Gandhi; not recorded as education. The site now claims 35M users versus 3M on the YC page, a growth claim not independently verified. Search for outcome events found no Kaagaz news.
